result.markdown: --- title: "DATA100 Introduction to Data Analytics" subtitle: "Lecture 10: Fancy Words and Numbers" author: "Agassi Iu" institute: "Wilfrid Laurier University" date: "October 27, 2026" format: live-revealjs: resources: - data/sleep_survey_v2.csv theme: sky slide-number: true transition: slide incremental: true embed-resources: true # Embeds figures and libraries into a single portable HTML file filters: - live webr: packages: - ggplot2 - dplyr - tidyr - tibble - readr - stringr - forcats - purrr - scales - lubridate execute: echo: true warning: false # Hides warnings and package loading messages message: false fig-width: 7 fig-height: 4 fig-align: center --- ::: {.cell} ::: # The story ## A night in the life of a student {.center} Last lecture, about 4 in 10 `bedtime` answers were still unreadable. Today we will finish the job, then ask what the *clean* times tell us: 1. When do students go to bed? (*Regular expressions*, Chapter 15) 2. When do they wake up, and who is still awake at 1 AM? (*Dates and times*, Chapter 17) ::: {.cell context='setup'} ::: ::: {.cell autorun='true'} ```{webr} #| include: false #| autorun: true library(dplyr) library(tibble) library(ggplot2) library(tidyverse) library(readr) survey <- read.csv("data/sleep_survey_v2.csv", fileEncoding = "WINDOWS-1252") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ## Setup and data The data is the same sleep survey from Lectures 8 and 9. ```r library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(tibble); library(readr) library(ggplot2); library(stringr); library(forcats); library(lubridate) survey <- read_csv("data/sleep_survey_v2.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) ``` ::: {.cell} ```{webr} survey |> select(student_id, survey_date, bedtime, sleep_hours) |> head(8) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip title="Not everything fits in this 80-minute lecture"} I may leave some of the undiscussed functions or tools in an *appendix table* at the end of the slide deck. Each row will say what the tool does and which section of the chapter to read. You should definitely take a look at the text for more details. ::: # Part 1: Regular expressions ## When do students go to bed? {.smaller} Our goal: turn every typed `bedtime` into an hour and a minute on a 24-hour clock. | Step | Tool (Chapter 15) | |------|-------------------| | Test for a pattern | `str_detect()`, `regex(ignore_case = TRUE)` | | Describe a pattern | `\\d`, `[:.]`, `?`, `{1,2}`, `^`, `$`, `(am\|pm)` | | Tidy the text | `str_replace()`, `str_remove()` | | Pull the pieces out | `separate_wider_regex()` | | Decide the rules | `case_when()` (Lecture 8) | ## Does it match? :::{.callout-note title="`str_detect(x, pattern)`"} This function returns a logical vector. It takes a look at `x` and asks for the `pattern`. It returns a `TRUE` where the pattern is found. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{webr} x <- c("11:30 pm", "23:30", "midnight", "idk") str_detect(x, "pm") str_detect(x, "\\d") # "\\d" means digits (from 0 to 9) ``` ::: On the survey: ::: {.cell} ```{webr} survey |> count(has_pm = str_detect(bedtime, "pm")) ``` ::: ## Capital letters matter `"PM"` and `"pm"` are different to a regular expression. Wrap the pattern in `regex()` to ignore the case: ::: {.cell} ```{webr} survey |> count(exact_case = str_detect(bedtime, "pm")) survey |> count(any_case = str_detect(bedtime, regex("pm", ignore_case = TRUE))) ``` ::: - The second count finds more `TRUE`s: it also catches `PM` and `Pm` ## Building blocks of a pattern {.smaller} | Pattern | Matches | |---------|---------| | `.` | any **one** character | | `\\.` | a real dot | | `\\d` | one digit | | `[:.]` | a colon **or** a dot | | `?` | the piece before it is optional (0 or 1 times) | | `{1,2}` | the piece before it appears 1 or 2 times | | `^` and `$` | the start and the end of the string | | (am|pm) | `am` **or** `pm` | ::: {.callout-warning title="Two backslashes in R"} In an R string, a backslash must be **escaped**. To get the regex `\d`, you type `"\\d"`. To match a real dot, you type `"\\."`, because a plain `.` matches anything. ::: ## A pattern for the standard format `"11:30 pm"` is: one or two digits, a colon, two digits, an optional space, then `am` or `pm`. ::: {.cell} ```{webr} pattern <- "^\\d{1,2}:\\d{2} ?(am|pm)$" x <- c("11:30 pm", "11:30PM", "1:05 am", "23:30", "11.30 pm") str_detect(x, regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)) ``` ::: - `^` and `$` force the pattern to match the **whole** string - Without them, `"around 11:30 pm"` would also match ## How many bedtimes match? ::: {.cell} ```{webr} pattern <- "^\\d{1,2}:\\d{2} ?(am|pm)$" survey |> count(standard = str_detect(bedtime, regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE))) ``` ::: ## What is left? The trick with regular expressions: look at what does **not** match, and improve the pattern. ::: {.cell} ```{webr} survey |> filter(!str_detect(bedtime, regex("^\\d{1,2}:\\d{2} ?(am|pm)$", ignore_case = TRUE))) |> count(bedtime, sort = TRUE) ``` ::: ## Cleaning - `str_replace(x, pattern, replacement)` replaces the **first** match - `str_remove(x, pattern)` deletes it - `str_replace_all()` replaces **every** match (see the appendix) ::: {.cell} ```{webr} x <- c(" Around 11:30PM", "~12:30am-ish", "11.30 p.m.", "midnight") x |> str_trim() |> str_to_lower() |> str_remove("^(around|about|~) ?") |> str_remove("-ish$") |> str_replace("midnight", "12:00 am") |> str_replace("p\\.m\\.", "pm") |> str_replace("\\.", ":") ``` ::: ## Apply the rules to the survey ::: {.cell} ```{webr} survey |> mutate( clean = str_to_lower(str_trim(bedtime)), clean = str_remove(clean, "^(around|about|~) ?"), clean = str_remove(clean, "-ish$"), clean = str_replace(clean, "midnight", "12:00 am"), clean = str_replace(clean, "a\\.m\\.", "am"), clean = str_replace(clean, "p\\.m\\.", "pm"), clean = str_replace(clean, "\\.", ":") ) |> count(standard = str_detect(clean, "^\\d{1,2}(:\\d{2})? ?(am|pm)$")) ``` ::: - Many more rows match, and we did not touch the data by hand - The rest are 24-hour times, times with no `am` or `pm`, and answers like `idk` ## Pulling the pieces out ::: {.callout-note title="`separate_wider_regex()`"} Last lecture we split on a space. A regular expression can split on a *pattern*. Each named piece becomes a column; unnamed pieces are matched and dropped. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{webr} df <- tibble(clean = c("11:30 pm", "2330", "11 pm", "12:00 am", "idk")) df |> separate_wider_regex( clean, patterns = c( hh = "\\d{1,2}", ":?", mm = "\\d{0,2}", " ?", ampm = "am|pm|" ), too_few = "align_start" ) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip title="Optional pieces"} `\\d{0,2}` allows **no** minutes, and the empty option at the end of `am|pm|` allows **no** `am` or `pm`. Strings that do not fit at all, like `idk`, become `NA`. ::: ## Deciding the rules ::: {.callout-tip title="We need rules!"} Some answers have no `am` or `pm`: `23:30`, `0100`, or just `11:30`. If it is - Already 24-hour (13 to 23, or 0): keep the hour - 6 to 11 with no `am` or `pm`: assume **evening** (add 12) - 12 or 1 to 5 with no `am` or `pm`: assume **after midnight** ::: ::: {.cell} ```{webr} df <- tibble(hh = c(11, 11, 23, 1, 12), ampm = c("pm", "", "", "", "")) df |> mutate( hour24 = case_when( ampm == "am" ~ hh %% 12, ampm == "pm" ~ hh %% 12 + 12, hh >= 13 | hh == 0 ~ hh, hh >= 6 & hh <= 11 ~ hh + 12, hh <= 5 | hh == 12 ~ hh %% 12 ) ) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-important title="Order matters"} `case_when()` uses the first match, as we talked about this with *Logical Vectors*. The 24-hour rule comes before the "6 to 11" rule for a reason. ::: ## Putting Part 1 together ::: {.cell autorun='true'} ```{webr} #| autorun: TRUE survey_clean <- survey |> mutate( clean = str_to_lower(str_trim(bedtime)), clean = str_remove(clean, "^(around|about|~) ?"), clean = str_remove(clean, "-ish$"), clean = str_replace(clean, "midnight", "12:00 am"), clean = str_replace(clean, "a\\.m\\.", "am"), clean = str_replace(clean, "p\\.m\\.", "pm"), clean = str_replace(clean, "\\.", ":") ) |> separate_wider_regex( clean, patterns = c(hh = "\\d{1,2}", ":?", mm = "\\d{0,2}", " ?", ampm = "am|pm|"), too_few = "align_start" ) |> mutate( hh = as.numeric(hh), mm = if_else(mm == "", 0, as.numeric(mm)), hour24 = case_when( ampm == "am" ~ hh %% 12, ampm == "pm" ~ hh %% 12 + 12, hh >= 13 | hh == 0 ~ hh, hh >= 6 & hh <= 11 ~ hh + 12, hh <= 5 | hh == 12 ~ hh %% 12 ) ) survey_clean |> summarize( readable = sum(!is.na(hour24)), blank = sum(is.na(bedtime)), unreadable = sum(is.na(hour24) & !is.na(bedtime)) ) ``` ::: ## The answer so far ::: {.cell} ```{webr} survey_clean |> filter(!is.na(hour24)) |> mutate( bed_hour = hour24 + mm / 60, bed_hour = if_else(bed_hour < 12, bed_hour + 24, bed_hour) ) |> ggplot(aes(x = bed_hour)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, boundary = 0, closed = "left") + facet_wrap(~ program) + scale_x_continuous( breaks = c(21, 24, 27), labels = c("9 PM", "12 AM", "3 AM") ) + labs( title = "Bedtimes by program", x = "Bedtime", y = "Students" ) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) ``` ::: - This is last lecture's plot, with half-hour bins and **many more** students - Engineering goes to bed later than Arts ::: {.callout-note title="What is still missing?"} Blank answers and answers like `idk` are still `NA`. We cannot recover what students did not tell us. ::: ## Aside: What happens to the rest of the unused responses? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} survey_clean |> filter(is.na(hour24)) |> count(bedtime, sort = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 7 × 2 bedtime n 1 23 2 it changes 8 3 no set time 7 4 varies 6 5 n/a 5 6 depends 4 7 idk 4 ``` ::: ::: ## Exercise 1 ::: {.callout-tip title="Live exercise"} 1. Count the bedtimes written as **four digits** with an optional colon, like `23:30` or `2330`. 2. Find every bedtime that contains the word `midnight` in **any capitalisation**, and count each spelling. ::: ::: {.cell exercise='ex_regex'} ```{webr} #| exercise: ex_regex # Part 1 survey |> count(four_digits = ) # Part 2 survey |> filter() |> count(bedtime) ``` ::: ::: {.cell exercise='ex_regex' solution='true'} ```{webr} #| exercise: ex_regex #| solution: true # Part 1: this also matches an unmarked time like 11:30 survey |> count(four_digits = str_detect(str_trim(bedtime), "^\\d{2}:?\\d{2}$")) # Part 2 survey |> filter(str_detect(bedtime, regex("midnight", ignore_case = TRUE))) |> count(bedtime) ``` ::: # Part 2: Dates and times ## When do they wake up? Wake-up time is **bedtime plus sleep**. To add them we need real date-times, just not text! | Step | Tool (Chapter 17) | |------|-------------------| | Create date-times | `ymd()`, `ymd_hms()`, `make_datetime()` | | Get the pieces | `hour()`, `minute()`, `wday()` | | Add time | `hours()`, `dhours()` | | Test for overlap | `interval()`, `%within%` | | Fix the time zone | `force_tz()`, `with_tz()` | ## Creating date-times from text The function name spells the **order** of the pieces: ::: {.cell} ```{webr} ymd("2026-10-27") mdy("October 27, 2026") dmy("27-Oct-2026") ymd_hms("2026-10-27 14:32:05") ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip title="Any separator works"} `ymd()` ignores dashes, slashes, and spaces. Only the order of year, month and day matters. ::: ## Creating date-times from parts ::: {.callout-note title="`make_datetime()`"} This function builds a date-time from separate numbers. Adding *periods* such as `hours()` moves the clock forward. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{webr} make_datetime(2026, 10, 27, 23, 30) # 25 hours after midnight on Oct 27 is 1 AM on Oct 28 make_datetime(2026, 10, 27) + hours(25) + minutes(30) ``` ::: - This is how we handle bedtimes *after midnight*: add 24 hours, and the date rolls over ## Bedtime as a date-time We pick one reference night (e.g. *October 27, 2026*), and add the hour and minute: ::: {.cell} ```{webr} survey_clean |> filter(!is.na(hour24)) |> mutate( bedtime_dt = make_datetime(2026, 10, 27, tz = "America/Toronto") + hours(if_else(hour24 < 12, hour24 + 24, hour24)) + minutes(mm) ) |> select(student_id, bedtime, bedtime_dt) ``` ::: - Use `if_else()` to add 24 to the after-midnight hours - `tz = "America/Toronto"` is the time zone. More on that soon ## Getting the pieces back ::: {.cell} ```{webr} t <- ymd_hms("2026-10-27 06:35:00") hour(t) minute(t) wday(t, label = TRUE) month(t) ``` ::: :::{.callout-warning title="Checkpoint"} What is the difference between `wday(t)` and `day(t)`? ::: ## Time spans ::: {.callout-tip title="Two way to add time"} - **Durations** (`dhours()`, `ddays()`) are an exact number of seconds - **Periods** (`hours()`, `days()`) move the **clock** by a calendar amount ::: ::: {.callout-caution title="When to use it?"} - Use *durations* for how long something lasts, like sleep. - Use *periods* for calendar time. ::: ## Daylight Savings Toronto switches to daylight saving time on November 1, 2026 starting at midnight. ::: {.cell} ```{webr} start <- ymd_hms("2026-11-01 00:00:00", tz = "America/Toronto") start + days(1) start + ddays(1) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-important title="Which one should I use?"} `days(1)` gives midnight on November 2 where the clock moved one day. `ddays(1)` gives *11 PM*: exactly 24 hours later, but the clocks jumped back in 1 hour. ::: ## Duration ::: {.callout-important title="Quick Maths"} `Wake-up time = bedtime + sleep`. Sleep is a duration, so we use `dhours()`. ::: ::: {.cell autorun='true'} ```{webr} #| autorun: TRUE sleep_times <- survey_clean |> filter(!is.na(hour24), !is.na(sleep_hours)) |> mutate( bedtime_dt = make_datetime(2026, 10, 27, tz = "America/Toronto") + hours(if_else(hour24 < 12, hour24 + 24, hour24)) + minutes(mm), wake = bedtime_dt + dhours(sleep_hours), wake_clock = hour(wake) + minute(wake) / 60 ) sleep_times |> select(student_id, bedtime_dt, sleep_hours, wake) ``` ::: ## Do students with an early class wake up earlier? ::: {.cell} ```{webr} sleep_times |> mutate(early = if_else(has_early_class == "Yes", "Has an early class", "No early class")) |> filter(!is.na(early)) |> ggplot(aes(x = wake_clock)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, boundary = 0, closed = "left") + facet_wrap(~ early, ncol = 1) + scale_x_continuous( breaks = 4:10, labels = c("4 AM", "5 AM", "6 AM", "7 AM", "8 AM", "9 AM", "10 AM") ) + labs( title = "Students with an early class wake up earlier", x = "Wake-up time", y = "Students" ) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) ``` ::: ## Average wake-up time ::: {.cell} ```{webr} sleep_times |> filter(!is.na(has_early_class)) |> group_by(has_early_class) |> summarize(mean_wake = mean(wake_clock)) |> mutate( hours = mean_wake %/% 1, minutes = round((mean_wake %% 1) * 60) ) ``` ::: ## Who is asleep at 1 AM? :::{.callout-note title="Interval"} The stretch of time between two date-times. `x %within% interval` is `TRUE` when `x` falls inside the interval. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{webr} asleep <- sleep_times |> mutate( sleeping = interval(bedtime_dt, wake), asleep_1am = make_datetime(2026, 10, 28, 1, tz = "America/Toronto") %within% sleeping ) asleep |> count(asleep_1am) ``` ::: ## Who is asleep at 1 AM? ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](DATA100-F26-Lecture-10_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-30-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Code ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](DATA100-F26-Lecture-10_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-31-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Better sleep = better grades? ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](DATA100-F26-Lecture-10_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-32-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sleep_times |> mutate( after_midnight = bedtime_dt > make_datetime(2026, 10, 28, tz = "America/Toronto") ) |> filter(!is.na(avg_grade)) |> ggplot(aes(x = sleep_hours, y = avg_grade, colour = after_midnight)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + scale_colour_manual( values = c("FALSE" = "grey60", "TRUE" = "firebrick"), labels = c("Bed before midnight", "Awake after midnight"), name = NULL ) + labs( title = "Sleep and grades, by bedtime", x = "Hours of sleep", y = "Average grade" ) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) ``` ::: ## What does the scatter plot say? ::: {.callout-caution title="What is after midnight?"} We used `>`, so a student at exactly 12:00 AM counts as **before** midnight. Change it to `>=` and see what happens. Boundaries matter, as with `cut()` last lecture. ::: ::: {.callout-tip title="Observations"} The red points sit to the left: students who go to bed after midnight sleep less. They also have slightly lower grades, but the two clouds overlap a lot. ::: ## Exercise 2 ::: {.callout-tip title="Live exercise"} Suppose that I have given you a tiny data set of three students. Their bedtime is a date-time, and sleep is in hours. 1. Compute each student's wake-up time. 2. Is each student asleep at 3:00 AM on October 28? 3. What share of the three students is asleep at 3:00 AM? ::: ::: {.cell exercise='ex_dates'} ```{webr} #| exercise: ex_dates df <- tibble( student = c("A", "B", "C"), bedtime = ymd_hms( c("2026-10-27 23:30:00", "2026-10-28 00:45:00", "2026-10-28 03:15:00"), tz = "America/Toronto" ), sleep_hours = c(7.5, 6, 4.25) ) df |> mutate( wake = , asleep_3am = ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell exercise='ex_dates' solution='true'} ```{webr} #| exercise: ex_dates #| solution: true df <- tibble( student = c("A", "B", "C"), bedtime = ymd_hms( c("2026-10-27 23:30:00", "2026-10-28 00:45:00", "2026-10-28 03:15:00"), tz = "America/Toronto" ), sleep_hours = c(7.5, 6, 4.25) ) df2 <- df |> mutate( wake = bedtime + dhours(sleep_hours), asleep_3am = make_datetime(2026, 10, 28, 3, tz = "America/Toronto") %within% interval(bedtime, wake) ) df2 # Student C goes to bed at 3:15, after 3:00, so only 2 of 3 are asleep df2 |> summarize(share_asleep = mean(asleep_3am)) ``` ::: # Wrap-up ## Summary | Question | Chapter | Tools we used | |----------|---------|---------------| | When do they go to bed? | *Regular expressions* | `str_detect()`, `str_replace()`, `str_remove()`, `separate_wider_regex()` | | When do they wake up, and who is awake at 1 AM? | *Dates and times* | `make_datetime()`, `hours()`, `dhours()`, `interval()`, `%within%` | ## What's next, and sources ::: {.callout-caution title="Lecture 11: Missing values and joins"} - **Missing values**: filling gaps, like the hours with no responses - **Joins**: bringing the drinks table into the survey ::: ::: {.callout-note title="Attribution"} Content adapted from *R for Data Science (2e)* by Hadley Wickham, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel, and Garrett Grolemund: - Chapter 15: Regular expressions, - Chapter 17: Dates and times, ::: # Appendix: read the text ## Regular expressions: other tools (i) {.smaller} | Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on | |------|--------------|--------------|---------------------| | `str_count()` | Counts how many times a pattern appears in each string | `str_count("banana", "a")` | Counting matches | | `str_extract()` | Pulls out the matching text itself | `str_extract("11:30 pm", "\\d+")` | Extracting | | `str_replace_all()` | Replaces **every** match, not just the first | `str_replace_all("a.b.c", "\\.", "-")` | Replacing values | ## Regular expressions: other tools (ii) {.smaller} | Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on | |------|--------------|--------------|---------------------| | `str_view()` | Shows where a pattern matches, highlighted | `str_view(x, "pm")` | Pattern basics | | Back references: `\\1` | Reuses the text a group captured | `str_replace(x, "(\\d+)h", "\\1 hours")` | Grouping and capturing | | `fixed()` | Matches the exact text, with no special characters | `str_detect(x, fixed("."))` | Fixed matches | ## Regular expressions: other tools (iii) {.smaller} | Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on | |------|--------------|--------------|---------------------| | `regex()` flags | `multiline`, `comments`, and more | `regex("pm", ignore_case = TRUE)` | Pattern control | | `+`, `*` | One or more, zero or more | `"\\d+"` | Quantifiers | | `[^...]` | Anything **except** these characters | `"[^0-9]"` | Character classes | ## Regular expressions: other tools (iv) {.smaller} | Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on | |------|--------------|--------------|---------------------| | `\\s`, `\\w` | A space; a letter, digit or underscore | `"\\s+"` | Character classes | | Parentheses | Control the order of `\|` and quantifiers | `"(am|pm)$"` | Operator precedence | ## Dates and times: other tools (i) {.smaller} | Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on | |------|--------------|--------------|---------------------| | `make_date()` | Builds a date from year, month and day | `make_date(2026, 10, 6)` | Creating date-times | | `as_datetime()`, `as_date()` | Converts between a date and a date-time | `as_date(now())` | Creating date-times | | `yday()`, `mday()` | Day of the year, day of the month | `yday(ymd("2026-10-06"))` | Getting components | | `round_date()`, `ceiling_date()` | Round to the nearest unit, or up | `ceiling_date(x, "hour")` | Rounding | ## Dates and times: other tools (ii) {.smaller} | Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on | |------|--------------|--------------|---------------------| | `update()` | Changes one component of a date-time | `update(x, hour = 6)` | Modifying components | | `as.duration()` | Turns a time difference into a duration | `as.duration(end - start)` | Durations | | `%--%` | A shortcut for `interval()` | `start %--% end` | Intervals | ## Dates and times: other tools (iii) {.smaller} | Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on | |------|--------------|--------------|---------------------| | `int_length()` | The length of an interval in seconds | `int_length(sleeping)` | Intervals | | `Sys.timezone()` | Your computer's time zone | `Sys.timezone()` | Time zones | ::: {.callout-tip title="Everything has a time zone"} Date-times without an explicit time zone are treated as **UTC**. Always check with `tz()` before you compute hours. :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
